(B) Firm, brief handshake with direct eye contact

question_en: What is 'Walpurgisnacht' in German folklore?
options: (B) Night of April 30 when witches were said to gather; celebrated with bonfires

question_en: In German restaurant culture, how do you typically request the bill?
options: (A) Stand up and walk to the cashier without asking
(B) Make eye contact with server and say 'Zahlen, bitte' or 'Die Rechnung, bitte'

question_en: Why is 'Pünktlichkeit' (punctuality) so emphasized in German culture?
options: (B) Strong cultural value linking punctuality with respect, reliability, and trustworthiness
(C) German clocks run faster than international time

question_en: What is 'Kindergarten' literally and culturally in Germany?
options: (B) 'Children's garden' — preschool tradition originating in Germany; ages ~3-6

question_en: In Germany, why are 'Vereine' (clubs/associations) so popular?
options: (B) Strong tradition of organized civic life — clubs for sports, hobbies, music, charity
(C) Only one club exists in Germany
(D) Clubs are banned and operate illegally

question_en: What does the German phrase 'das ist nicht mein Bier' mean?
When invited to a Polish home, what is the traditional welcome gesture?
options: (A) A formal handshake at the door only
(B) Greeted with bread and salt (chleb i sól) — symbol of hospitality
(C) Removing your shoes and giving them to the host

question_en: What is 'Imieniny' in Polish culture?
options: (B) Name day — celebrating the saint's day matching your name, often more important than birthdays

question_en: Why is 'Wigilia' (Christmas Eve) so significant in Polish tradition?
options: (B) Most important meal of the year — 12 meatless dishes, sharing opłatek wafer, watch for first star
(C) Same as American Christmas, no special meaning

question_en: At a Polish Wigilia dinner table, why is one extra place setting traditionally left empty?
options: (B) For an unexpected guest, lonely traveler, or in memory of absent family
(D) Polish tradition does not include this practice

question_en: What is 'Śmigus-Dyngus' on Easter Monday in Poland?
options: (B) Wet Monday — playful water-throwing tradition between people, especially among young people

question_en: When meeting a Polish woman formally, what was a traditional respectful greeting (especially with older generations)?
options: (B) Kissing her hand (całowanie w rękę) — traditional gesture of respect

question_en: Why is bread (chleb) considered sacred in Polish culture?
options: (A) Bread is rare and expensive in Poland
(B) Symbol of God's gift, life, and family; should never be wasted or dropped on the floor

question_en: What does saying 'Smacznego' mean in Polish dining etiquette?
options: (A) 'Thank you for the meal' after eating
(B) 'Bon appétit' — said before starting a meal
(C) 'I am full and cannot eat more'

question_en: Why do Poles typically bring an odd number of flowers (not even) when giving them?
options: (A) Polish florists only sell odd numbers
(B) Even-numbered bouquets are traditionally for funerals/cemeteries
(C) Polish currency is denominated in odd numbers

question_en: What is 'Wszystkich Świętych' (All Saints' Day, November 1) in Polish culture?
options: (A) A small religious observance ignored by most
(B) Major national holiday — families visit graves, light candles, remember the deceased
(D) The first day of winter celebrations

question_en: When toasting with vodka in Poland, what is traditional etiquette?
options: (A) Sip slowly over the course of an hour
(B) Maintain eye contact, say 'Na zdrowie' (to health), and traditionally drink in one shot
(C) Pour the vodka on the floor first
(D) Drink it mixed with juice only

question_en: What is the formal address 'Pan/Pani' used for in Polish?
options: (B) 'Mr./Mrs.' — used as a respectful third-person address even when speaking directly

question_en: Why are pierogi central to Polish food culture?
options: (A) They are only eaten once a year
(B) Traditional dumplings with many fillings (cheese-potato, meat, mushroom, sweet) — a comfort food staple
(C) They are an American invention falsely attributed to Poland

question_en: Why is mushroom picking (grzybobranie) a major Polish autumn tradition?
options: (A) Mushrooms are the only food in Poland
(B) Cultural tradition combining family time, forest visits, foraging knowledge, and food preservation
(C) Mushrooms are a recent food trend

question_en: At a Polish birthday or name day, what song is traditionally sung?
options: (B) 'Sto lat!' (100 years!) — wishing 100 years of life

question_en: What is Poland's relationship with Pope John Paul II (Karol Wojtyła)?
options: (A) He is a minor historical figure rarely mentioned
(B) National hero and saint — first Polish pope, key cultural and spiritual icon
(C) He was Polish but disliked in Poland

question_en: Why is the Solidarity (Solidarność) movement important to Polish identity?
options: (B) Trade union led by Lech Wałęsa that contributed to ending communist rule in Poland

question_en: What does the informal greeting 'Cześć' mean in Polish?
options: (B) Casual 'Hi/Hello' or 'Bye' used among friends and peers

question_en: Why do many Poles cross themselves when passing a church?
options: (A) It is required by Polish law
(B) Catholic tradition reflecting deep religious heritage (~85% Catholic identification)

question_en: What is 'bigos' in Polish cuisine?
options: (B) Hunter's stew — sauerkraut, fresh cabbage, various meats; often tastes better reheated
(C) A cold soup served only in summer

question_en: At a traditional Polish wedding, what is the 'Polonez' (Polonaise)?
options: (B) The first dance — a stately processional dance opening the reception

question_en: Why is 'Babcia' (grandmother) a respected and central figure in Polish families?
options: (A) Babcias are typically distant from family
(B) Often a primary caregiver, cultural transmitter of recipes, language, and family memory
(C) Polish tradition excludes grandmothers from family life

question_en: What is the Polish tradition of 'opłatek'?
options: (B) Christmas wafer shared at Wigilia — family breaks pieces and exchanges wishes
(D) A type of Polish folk music

question_en: Why is 8 March (Dzień Kobiet, Women's Day) marked in Poland?
options: (B) Tradition of giving women small gifts (especially flowers like tulips); Soviet-era origin, still popular

question_en: What is 'kompot' served with Polish meals?
options: (B) A drink made from boiled fruits, served warm or cold, often homemade

question_en: Why are Polish funerals often quite solemn and full of religious symbolism?
options: (B) Strong Catholic tradition with Masses, processions, mourning rituals, and church involvement
(C) Polish funerals are typically celebratory parties
(D) Funerals are kept secret in Polish culture

question_en: What does 'Solenizant' refer to in Polish celebrations?
options: (B) The person whose name day or birthday is being celebrated — center of the event
(C) The host who pays the bill

question_en: Why is volleyball (siatkówka) such a passion in Poland?
options: (A) It is illegal there, so people sneak away to play it
(B) Polish national teams have a long record of success; widely followed as a major sport
(D) Only one volleyball court exists in Poland

question_en: What is 'Krakow vs Warsaw' in Polish cultural identity?
options: (A) Two villages of equal small size
(B) Friendly rivalry between historic royal/cultural capital (Krakow) and modern political/financial capital (Warsaw)
(C) Names of two soccer teams only

question_en: In Polish toasting culture, what does refusing the next round (kolejka) typically mean?
options: (B) Can be seen as breaking the social rhythm; pressure to continue is common, though declining is increasingly accepted

question_en: Why is the Polish phrase 'Nie ma sprawy' commonly used?
Why is 'Constitution Day' (3 maja) a national holiday in Poland?
options: (B) Commemorates the 1791 Constitution, second written national constitution in the world after the U.S.
(C) The day Poland was founded in 2000

question_en: What is 'oscypek' in Polish regional culture?
options: (B) Smoked sheep's-milk cheese from the Tatra mountains, EU-protected origin

question_en: What is the cultural meaning of giving someone yellow chrysanthemums in Poland?
options: (B) Funerals and All Saints' Day — for cemeteries, not romantic gestures

question_en: Why do many Poles still consider it customary to remove shoes at home?
options: (B) Practical (mud, snow) and cultural cleanliness norm; hosts often offer slippers (kapcie)
(D) The custom does not exist in Poland

question_en: What is 'Andrzejki' (St. Andrew's Eve, November 29)?
options: (B) Folk fortune-telling night, especially for young unmarried women (e.g., pouring melted wax through a keyhole)

question_en: Why is 'kotlet schabowy' a Polish staple?
options: (A) It is a rare delicacy reserved for royalty
(B) Breaded pork cutlet, common home and restaurant dish, often with potatoes and cabbage

question_en: When a Polish person says 'może' ('maybe'), what does it often mean in social contexts?
options: (B) Genuine uncertainty or a soft/polite way to decline without saying 'no' directly

question_en: Why do Polish weddings traditionally last very long, sometimes 2+ days?
options: (B) Cultural emphasis on extended family celebration, food, drink, dance, and rituals
(C) Weddings are 30 minutes only in Poland
(D) Only one Polish wedding has ever lasted long

question_en: What is 'tłusty czwartek' (Fat Thursday) in Polish tradition?
options: (B) Last Thursday before Lent — eating pączki (filled donuts) and other rich foods

question_en: How do Polish drivers typically signal 'thank you' on the road?
options: (B) Briefly flashing hazard lights (or raising hand) after being let in or helped

question_en: Why are 'kapcie' (slippers) typically offered to guests in Polish homes?
options: (B) Standard part of removing-shoes hospitality — keeping feet warm and floors clean

question_en: What is the significance of 'Marian devotion' (e.g., Black Madonna of Częstochowa) in Polish Catholicism?
options: (B) Deeply central — Black Madonna is national symbol; Częstochowa pilgrimages are major events

question_en: Why is 'Polish hospitality' often described as overwhelming?
options: (A) Poles dislike guests and try to drive them away with food
(B) 'Gość w dom, Bóg w dom' (Guest at home, God at home) — generous tradition of feeding and serving guests

question_en: When asked 'jak się masz?' ('how are you?') in Polish, what is the typical response style?
options: (B) Often more honest than English equivalent — Poles may give a genuine answer about how they actually feel

question_en: What is 'kawa po turecku' in Polish coffee culture?
options: (B) Turkish-style coffee — ground beans steeped directly in hot water; traditional Polish home coffee

question_en: Why is 'Lajkonik' (parading hobby horse) a Krakow tradition?
options: (B) Annual June festival figure dressed as a Tatar warrior on a hobby horse, parading through Krakow

question_en: When eating dinner at someone's Polish home, what is rude?
options: (A) Eating all the food on your plate
(B) Refusing food persistently when offered; saying 'I am full' too early in the meal

question_en: Why is 'Adam Mickiewicz' a household name in Poland?
options: (B) National poet (1798-1855); his epic 'Pan Tadeusz' is foundational Polish literature

question_en: What does the saying 'Mądry Polak po szkodzie' mean culturally?
options: (B) 'A Pole is wise after the damage' — self-deprecating idiom about learning from mistakes too late
